title: India and Israel Elevate Ties to Special Strategic Partnership
excerpt: Modi's state visit to Israel yields 16 bilateral agreements spanning AI, defense, cybersecurity, and a framework for 50,000 Indian workers, as both nations push toward a free trade deal.
body:
• India and Israel elevated their relationship to a "Special Strategic Partnership for Peace, Innovation & Prosperity" during PM Modi's February 2026 state visit to Jerusalem.
  • The two nations signed 16 agreements covering AI, cybersecurity, defense, agriculture, a UPI-Israel payments linkage, and worker mobility protocols for up to 50,000 Indian workers over five years.
  • Both sides signed the terms of reference for a Free Trade Agreement and held the first round of negotiations, signaling intent to deepen economic integration.
  • The leaders condemned terrorism, including the October 7 attack on Israel and the Pahalgam attack in India, and discussed the Gaza peace process.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu agreed to elevate bilateral ties to a "Special Strategic Partnership for Peace, Innovation & Prosperity" during Modi's state visit to Israel on February 25-26, 2026. The upgrade, formalized in a joint statement, marks the most significant expansion of the India-Israel relationship since Modi's first visit to the country in 2017.

16 Agreements in Two Days

The visit produced 16 signed agreements spanning technology, defense, agriculture, education, and worker mobility. Among the most consequential: a memorandum of understanding on artificial intelligence cooperation, the establishment of an Indo-Israel Cyber Centre of Excellence in India, and the signing of terms of reference for a Free Trade Agreement — with the first round of negotiations already held in New Delhi.

"Had an excellent meeting with Prime Minister Netanyahu," Modi said in a post on X. "Sectors such as technology, water management, agriculture, talent partnership and more offer immense scope for close collaboration."

"The bond between India and Israel is a powerful alliance... he is coming here so that we can tighten it even more."

— Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel

Defense, Cyber, and Critical Technologies

Building on a defense cooperation MoU signed in November 2025, the leaders outlined a roadmap for expanded military collaboration. A new initiative on Critical and Emerging Technologies, led by the national security advisors of both countries, will focus on AI, semiconductors, quantum computing, and cybersecurity.

The cybersecurity component includes a multi-year strategic program with joint tabletop exercises, Security by Design principles, and human capacity building. India's growing defense imports from Israel — which have made it one of India's top three defense suppliers — provide the commercial backdrop for these commitments.

Economic Integration and Financial Links

The economic agenda extended beyond defense. A Bilateral Investment Treaty, signed by both finance ministers in September 2025, aims to boost two-way investment flows. Netanyahu praised India's Unified Payments Interface, and both sides agreed to explore linking UPI with Israel's MASAV payment system for cross-border transactions.

Both leaders also discussed the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) and expressed intent to advance Israel's role within the initiative, alongside the I2U2 quadrilateral partnership with the UAE and the United States.

Direct air connectivity between Tel Aviv and major Indian cities was identified as essential for scaling the relationship, with both leaders encouraging airlines to launch new routes.

Agriculture, Workers, and People-to-People Ties

Agriculture remains a cornerstone of the partnership. The leaders welcomed the establishment of the India-Israel Innovation Centre for Agriculture and noted that 35 centers of excellence are already operating across India, with more than one million Indian farmers trained through these programs.

In a significant move for the Indian diaspora, both leaders agreed that up to 50,000 additional Indian workers may arrive in Israel within the next five years, with new protocols covering the commerce, manufacturing, and restaurant sectors alongside existing construction and caregiver agreements.

"India deeply values the enduring friendship with Israel, built on trust, innovation and a shared commitment to peace and progress."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India

Counterterrorism and Regional Security

The joint statement condemned terrorism "in all its forms and manifestations," specifically referencing the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, the April 2025 Pahalgam attack in Indian-administered Kashmir, and a November 2025 incident near Red Fort in New Delhi. Both leaders discussed the Gaza peace process and welcomed the U.S. comprehensive plan to end the conflict.

Modi's visit — his second to Israel in nine years — came amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East, including deteriorating U.S.-Iran relations, lending additional diplomatic weight to the trip.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the estimated 85,000 Indians living and working in Israel, the worker mobility agreements and new sector protocols represent tangible improvements in legal protections and employment opportunities. The push for direct flights, expanded education exchanges including a new MoU between Nalanda University and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and the India-Israel Academic Cooperation Forum point to a relationship that is deepening well beyond the traditional defense-and-agriculture framework.
